meta.name: Detect idle device activity from Prey screenshots with Claude Vision

parameters.content:
## 1. Trigger & configuration

Webhook for production, manual trigger for testing. The analysis window lives in the Set node.

## 2. Cooldown, reports & window filter

Skips the run if the last analysis was less than cooldown_minutes ago. Otherwise fetches the device reports and keeps the ones inside the window — requiring min_reports screenshots spanning at least min_span_minutes — then samples down to max_images.

## 3. Download & Claude vision analysis

Downloads each screenshot as binary and sends the full set to the Anthropic API in a single request.

# Prey Idle detection from screenshots

## How it works
1. A Prey report arrives (webhook) or the workflow is run manually for testing
2. If the last analysis ran less than cooldown_minutes ago, the run exits early (skipped)
3. Device reports are fetched and the most recent one anchors the window
4. Reports within window_minutes are kept; the run needs at least min_reports screenshots spanning at least min_span_minutes, otherwise it stops with idle: null
5. Up to max_images screenshots (evenly sampled, first and last always included) are downloaded from the Prey panel
6. Claude vision compares the set, ignoring noise (clock, battery, notifications)
7. The verdict comes out as JSON: idle true/false, a summary, and the analyzed reports

## Setup
- [ ] Pick your device in the 'Get device reports' node (Prey account credential)
- [ ] Review the defaults in 'Set — Window config' (window, minimums, sampling, cooldown)
- [ ] Check the Anthropic credential on the Claude vision node

## Customize
- Change the model in 'Code — Build Claude vision request' (currently claude-haiku-4-5)
- Chain an action after 'Code — Activity verdict' (Slack, DB, etc.) using $json.idle

## Note
The cooldown uses workflow static data, which only persists in production executions — manual test runs are never blocked by it.
